instructions.question: Does this Facebook comment on the Kosovo public health institute's COVID-19 post express a clear emotional stance (warm approval/hope versus hostility/distress), or is it mainly informational, practical or joking?
instructions.rule: Neutral is the default and the largest class. Demands, suggestions, requests for data, 'why' questions, criticism of careless citizens or cafes, sarcasm about testing, jokes about cities 'leading the league', and 'ma gjall' cheering are all neutral, even when phrased sharply. Negative needs explicit hostility or distress: calling the numbers lies or a farce, curses or insults, or stated sadness, fear, despair or exhaustion. Positive needs clear praise, thanks, blessings or relief; praise mixed with criticism is still positive.

neutral.what: Name tags, jokes, banter, statistics, questions, requests for details, demands for measures or more tests, advice and criticism of citizens without insult or despair.
examples: Mbyllni kufinjt mos luani me jetet e njerzve (Close the borders, don't play with people's lives)
Pse nuk po perputhen rastet e juaja me ato raste qe i raportoni ne OBSh???? (Why don't your cases match those you report to WHO????)
Nëse nuk bëjmë asnjë test, s'do të kemi asnjë rast. U zgjidh problemi. (If we do no tests, we'll have no cases. Problem solved.)
Vushtria on top çdo nat (Vushtrria on top every night)
neutral.cues: pse (why), testoni (test), publikoni (publish), mbyllni (close), kthene karantinen (bring back quarantine), ma gjall (livelier), on top, hahaha, personal names
neutral.not_for: Explicit 'lies', curses, 'turp' aimed at the institute, or stated sadness or fear are negative.

positive.what: Praise or thanks to doctors or the institute, blessings, wishes for recovery, explicit relief or joy at recoveries or falling cases.
examples: Respekt per punen tuaj (Respect for your work)
Sherim te shpejt per te gjith. (Quick recovery to all.)
Mos e ndrroni prej ndrrimit qit doktor se mir pi hec (Don't change this doctor from the shift, he's doing well)
Mashallah kofshin me ymer (Mashallah, may they live long)
positive.cues: bravo (well done), respekt (respect), ju lumt (well done), faleminderit (thanks), Zoti ju bekoft (God bless you), sherim (recovery), shyqyr (thank God), kofshin me ymer (may they live long)
positive.not_for: Wishes for fewer cases, or jokes about a city being 'on top', are neutral.

negative.what: Claims that the numbers are lies or invented, curses and insults, explicit sadness, fear, despair or exhaustion, bitter hopelessness about Kosovo.
examples: Krejt Rrena (All lies)
Trishtim, 15 vdekje edhe dje. (Sadness, 15 deaths yesterday too.)
Bergamo e ballkanit jena bo ka 13 persona me vdek tmer i zotit osht (We've become the Bergamo of the Balkans, 13 people dying, it's God's horror)
Si gjithcka tjeter  edhe COVID 19 do te deshtoj ne Kosove (Like everything else, COVID 19 will fail in Kosovo too)
negative.cues: rrena/gënjeshtra (lies), hajgare (farce), zoti ju vraft (God curse you), flaka ju dalt (may you burn), trishtim (sadness), tmerr (horror), na lodhet (we're exhausted), magari (donkey)
negative.not_for: Practical demands, data questions, scolding people to wear masks, or sarcastic jokes without insult are neutral.
